{{chess-rules}}
{{representation-instructions}}
Treat the supplied current position as authoritative. Do not reconstruct the position from familiar openings, standard-chess assumptions, or remembered move sequences.
When the representation is numeric, use only the supplied piece names and absolute numeric coordinates.
A move is determined only by the actual source piece, destination, geometry, occupancy, supplied variant rules, and royal king safety. Compound pieces always retain every movement component listed in the rules.
Choose the move with the best chances of winning.
Before answering, silently verify the chosen move only: source piece and side, destination occupancy, exact dx and dy, movement rule, path or intermediate squares when relevant, capture or special-move conditions, and royal king safety. Also check whether the moved piece can be captured immediately on its destination and whether that would simply lose material without sufficient compensation. If the move fails any check, choose another.
Do not output analysis, calculations, alternatives, explanations, or commentary.
